About AccuGeo

AccuGeo Liner, Inc. is a fabricator of quality, dependable geomembranes. We use our specialized expertise in the geomembrane industry to help our clients deliver their projects on time and on budget.

You can build your professional reputation on quality of materials, service and technical assistance at AccuGeo. We offer a wide variety of geomembrane materials to meet your company's individual containment needs.

AccuGeo focuses on manufacturing high quality liners and supporting our customers as they focus on high quality installations. We do not compete with our customers. We produce the best possible solution for you.

<#-- title: PVC -->

PVC Liners

PVC is durable and easy to use, making it a perfect liner for beginners. Adhesive will seam and patch PVC and requires no expensive equipment.

PVC liners should be buried, the same as PVC pipe. PVC has carbon black as a UV inhibitor, however prolonged UV exposure will degrade PVC over time. Buried PVC liners will have a life of 20 years or more. Exposed PVC liners last a few months to a year, depending on the thickness of the liner.

PVC roll stock is 7.083 feet wide. After subtracting for the seam, the width of the liner panels will be in increments of 7'. For example, a panel could be 14' wide or 21' wide, etc. The maximum panel width is 140'. The length can be any value.

At a glance

Standard thicknesses
10, 20, 30, 40, 60 mil
Panel width increments
7' (max 140')
Seaming methods
RF welding, heat welding, adhesive
Standard warranty
20 years when buried (not on 10 mil)
Minimum order
None

<#-- title: HDPE -->

HDPE Liners

HDPE (High Density Polyethylene) is a special form of polyethylene that has longer carbon strings with less branching. The result is a more compactable molecule and a higher density. HDPE is available smooth or with texturing called Microspike® to increase the slip coefficient.

HDPE is shipped in large rolls and mechanically deployed. All seams are made in the field using heat fusion or a tape designed for geosynthetics. HDPE is slightly less expensive than other materials, but has a higher cost of installation. It can be cost effective in large projects. HDPE should only be installed by qualified professionals.

At a glance

Standard thicknesses
12, 20, 30, 40, 60, 80, 100 mil
Roll width
19' (12–20 mil), 23' (other)
Seaming methods
Heat welding, tape
Standard warranty
1 year, extensions available
Minimum order
None

Microspike® is a registered trademark of Agru America, Inc.

<#-- title: EPDM -->

EPDM Liners

EPDM (Ethylene Propylene Diene Terpolymer) is a synthetic rubber, which gives it much more elasticity than other liner materials. EPDM is a beginner-friendly material that is most common in small koi ponds, with excellent resistance to UV and harsh environmental conditions.

Pipe penetrations are made easily by cutting an undersized hole and stretching the liner over the pipe. Note that the hole must be round to evenly distribute the stress around the circumference.

At a glance

Standard thickness
45 mil
Standard roll sizes
10'–50' wide, 100'–200' long
Seaming method
Tape
Minimum order
None, partial rolls available

<#-- title: Lakes & Ponds -->

Lake and Pond Liners

Lakes and ponds transform otherwise boring property into beautiful terrain. Upgrading your landscape is easy even for beginners with AccuGeo's liners. Installing a liner can be intimidating at first, but many times it is as simple as unfolding a liner and pulling it into place.

The two most popular materials for lake and pond liners are PVC and Polypropylene. These materials are reliable, inexpensive and easy to install. Use PVC if you are going to bury the liner and make the pond look natural. Use Polypropylene if any part of the liner will be exposed to sunlight.

PVC is easy to patch with adhesive and costs less, but degrades from the ultraviolet rays (UV) in sunlight. Polypropylene has excellent UV resistance, but has to be patched with a hot air welder. Some pond designers prefer to use polypropylene in case the liner accidentally becomes exposed to sunlight for an extended period.

Plan your pond with us

<#-- title: Potable Water -->

Potable Water Liners

Potable water is water that must be safe for human consumption. Check local regulations for the liner materials approved for use in your area.

Most areas require that liners for potable water are certified by the National Sanitation Foundation (NSF) to meet the NSF/ANSI 61 standard. NSF certified liners are inspected to ensure that all ingredients, including the polymer and additives such as UV stabilizers, heat stabilizers and antioxidants, are safe for contact with drinking water.

Common liner materials for potable water are NSF certified 36 and 45 mil Polypropylene.

Ask about NSF certified liners

<#-- title: Canals -->

Canal Liners

Canal liners are a cost effective solution whether you want to replace traditional concrete or just be prepared when it cracks. Plastic liners are a fraction of the cost of concrete and completely stop seepage losses. However, care should be taken to protect the liner from animals, vandalism and other potential damage. The canal liner can be protected with a layer of backfill or by placing the liner under a traditional concrete canal.

AccuGeo can custom fabricate long canal liners that are cheap and easy to install as a large panel. PVC is a popular choice for canal liners under concrete or backfill. Polypropylene and HDPE are popular choices for liners that will be left exposed.

Both Polypropylene and HDPE will float on water if the liner gets a leak. This can lead to bank erosion if the liner is not weighted down to prevent water from flowing under the liner.
